Course 17

Brain and behaviour

Neurons, brain regions, plasticity and what neuroscience can and cannot tell us.

Lesson 2. A tour of the brain

1 · Lesson

The brainstem regulates vital functions such as breathing and heart rate. The cerebellum coordinates movement and takes part in skill learning. Deep inside, the limbic system (with structures such as the amygdala and hippocampus) is involved in emotion and memory.

The cerebral cortex is divided into four lobes: frontal (planning, impulse control, voluntary movement, speech), parietal (touch and spatial orientation), temporal (hearing, language comprehension, memory) and occipital (vision).

This division is useful but simplified: almost any complex activity recruits networks connecting many regions. Differences between hemispheres exist (language is usually more lateralised to the left), but the idea of "left-brained" or "right-brained" people has no basis.

2 · Example

Phineas Gage, a railway foreman, survived an iron rod passing through his frontal lobe in 1848. According to accounts, his character changed. The case has been exaggerated over the years, but it helped link the frontal lobe to personality and self-control.

3 · Activity

Draw a brain from the side from memory and mark the four lobes and the cerebellum. Then compare it with a reliable image and correct what is needed.
